    Interdisciplinary computational social scientist (and musician).
    
    
I have a background in psychology, behavioral sciences and sociology. In my PhD I researched participation in community energy projects through a combination of social network analysis, computational methods and participatory modelling as part of the NNC cluster embedded in the Sociology department of the University of Groningen. 

In recent studies I investigated the diffusion potential of different seeding strategies through empirically informed diffusion models and more theoretical Agent Based Models. On the more applied side of things, I conducted a networked co-creation project with two community energy projects to collectively devise dissemination strategies. 

In the past I researched social interactions with and perceptions of robots at the Behavior Science institute in Nijmegen and I investigated behavior change interventions to promote sustainable food choices at the institute for Environmental Psychology in Vienna. In my bachelor’s I delved into computational linguistics, studying how kinematic movements support verbal communication, at the Max Plank institute for linguistics in Nijmegen. 

That said I have broad interest in social scientific topics and beyond and I am eager to learn new methodology. Here a few keywords describing my current research interest: social network analysis; simulations; ABM; diffusion of innovations; energy transition; networks and sustainability; behavior change; collective action; HRI.
